title: Business property sales — Kiran Patel
instructions: Kiran Patel, a sole proprietor, sold three business assets held over a year in 2025. He has no prior §1231 losses.

exhibits.title: Sales
exhibits.content:
- Equipment: cost **$80,000**; accumulated depreciation **$50,000**; sold for **$70,000**
- Building: cost **$500,000**; straight-line depreciation **$100,000**; sold for **$550,000**
- Land: basis **$120,000**; sold for **$100,000**

rows.label: §1245 ordinary income on the equipment
rows.explanation: Gain 40,000 (70,000 − 30,000) is all recapture, up to 50,000 of depreciation: **40,000**.

rows.label: Net §1231 gain
rows.explanation: 150,000 − 20,000 land loss = **130,000**, treated as long-term capital gain.

rows.label: Unrecaptured §1250 gain (25% maximum rate)
rows.explanation: Straight-line depreciation on the building, limited to the net §1231 gain: **100,000**.

rows.label: If Kiran had a $30,000 unrecaptured net §1231 loss from 2022, would part of this year's net §1231 gain be ordinary?
rows.explanation: The 5-year lookback recaptures prior net §1231 losses as ordinary income.

rows.label: Is there §1250 ordinary recapture on the building for an individual using straight-line depreciation?
rows.explanation: Only depreciation in excess of straight-line is §1250 ordinary recapture.
